Empirical Research Plan: “The Economic Impact of Conflict in the Basque Country”

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
Strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) complemented by an event-study (dynamic DID).

Justification  
• The treatment (onset/presence of conflict) affects only one region, while many comparable regions within the same country were not exposed.  
• We observe multiple years before and after conflict onset, allowing us to compare pre-trends and trace dynamic effects.  
• Spain’s regions share national institutions, monetary policy, and business-cycle shocks, so region and year fixed effects capture most common shocks.  
• The DID framework is easy to interpret and can be extended to an event-study to test the parallel-trend assumption and examine effect heterogeneity over time.

Why not RDD or IV?  No obvious running variable with a cutoff that determines conflict exposure; a credible external instrument is also hard to find.  DID with an event-study therefore fits naturally.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL DEFINITION
Treatment variable  
Treatedit = 1 if region i is the Basque Country AND year t ≥ 1968  
(where 1968 ≈ first large-scale ETA violent episode; adjust if using another commonly accepted start year). Treatedit = 0 otherwise.

Control group  
All other Spanish NUTS-2 regions that never experienced systematic separatist violence.  We exclude Navarre (violence spillovers) in the baseline but will include it in robustness checks.

Treatment timing  
Event (conflict onset) year = 1968.  We code an “event time” k = t − 1968 to build the event-study dummies.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS (DID)
A1. Parallel Pre-Trends: In the absence of conflict, GDP per capita in the Basque Country would have followed the same trend as in the control regions.  
Plausibility: The Basque Country was one of Spain’s richer regions pre-1968 but its growth trend was similar to other industrial regions (Catalonia, Madrid). We can empirically test this in the event-study’s lead coefficients.

A2. No Anticipation: Agents did not change economic behavior in advance of 1968 in anticipation of large-scale sustained conflict.  
Plausibility: Violence escalated relatively quickly; early isolated incidents existed but were small. Still, we test for significant pre-treatment dips in the 3–5 years before 1968.

A3. SUTVA / No Spillovers: Conflict in the Basque Country does not directly depress GDP per capita in control regions (or raise it through relocation).  
Plausibility: Some firms could relocate; we mitigate by dropping bordering Navarre and robustness-checking on remaining controls.

A4. Stable Composition: Region borders and GDP measurement methodology are constant across time.  
Plausibility: True for modern Spanish national accounts; the INE used consistent definitions post-1955.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
T1. Pre-existing Divergence (Violates A1)  
• Mitigation: (i) Event-study pre-trend test, (ii) include region-specific linear trends, (iii) synthetic-control robustness.

T2. Spillovers / Migration (Violates A3)  
• Mitigation: Drop neighboring provinces, re-run with progressively wider “exclusion zones.” Test net-migration flows; if strong, instrument Basque labor force with lagged fertility to purge migration effects.

T3. Concurrent Region-Specific Policy Shocks (e.g., fiscal autonomy laws in 1978)  
• Mitigation: Add interaction controls for the post-1978 Basque Statute; or restrict sample to pre-statute years in robustness; or difference-out by using “Basque minus Catalonia” (another autonomy region) differences.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R CODE OUTLINE

```r
# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-performance fixed-effects estimation
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load Data --------------------------------------------------------------
# Assume file regions_spain.csv in working directory
# key vars: region_id, year, gdp_pc, population, etc.
dat <- fread("regions_spain.csv")   

# 2. Variable Construction --------------------------------------------------
# Basque identifier
dat[, basque := as.integer(region_id == "Basque")]

# Treatment start year
t0 <- 1968

# DID dummy
dat[, post := as.integer(year >= t0)]
dat[, treat := basque * post]

# Event-time dummies for event study (k from −10 to +20)
for (k in -10:20){
  dat[, paste0("event_",k) := as.integer(basque == 1 & year == t0 + k)]
}

# 3. Baseline DID -----------------------------------------------------------
did_fit <- feols(gdp_pc ~ treat | region_id + year,   # two-way FE
                 data = dat, cluster = "region_id")
summary(did_fit)

# 4. Event Study ------------------------------------------------------------
# Drop one post period for identification (e.g., k = −1)
event_vars <- grep("^event_", names(dat), value = TRUE)
event_formula <- as.formula(paste(
  "gdp_pc ~", paste(event_vars, collapse = " + "),
  "| region_id + year"))
event_fit <- feols(event_formula, data = dat, cluster = "region_id")
coefplot(event_fit, drop = "event_-1") + theme_minimal()

# 5. Robustness Check: Region-Specific Trends ------------------------------
did_trend <- feols(gdp_pc ~ treat + i(year, basque, ref = 1967) | region_id, 
                   data = dat, cluster = "region_id")
summary(did_trend)
```
More checks you would add: placebo treatment dates, excluding Catalonia/Madrid, synthetic control (Synth package), GDP growth instead of level, etc.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. EXPECTED RESULTS
Direction: Negative.  Conflict should dampen GDP per capita growth due to reduced investment, brain drain, and higher security costs.  
Magnitude (rough prior): A cumulative loss of 5–10 percent of GDP per capita relative to counterfactual over the first 10 years, roughly −0.5 pp per year in growth rates.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)
(1 = clearly satisfied; 0 = questionable)

C1. No differential pre-treatment trend?  … 0.8  
C2. Treatment exogenous to potential outcomes? … 0.6  
C3. No spillovers or interference? … 0.5  
C4. Stable sample composition / measurement? … 1  
C5. Correct functional form / serial correlation handled (cluster)? … 0.9  

Total (out of 5): 3.8 → Acceptable but requires diligence on pre-trends and spillovers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This plan combines a simple yet rigorous DID with rich robustness checks to credibly estimate how conflict depressed the Basque Country’s economic trajectory.
